questions.q: Would you say you're a happy person?
questions.answer: I'd say so, yes. I have a supportive family, a job that feels meaningful and good health. I've learned not to [[take things for granted]], and that alone makes me feel quite fortunate most days.

questions.q: What kinds of things make you happy?
questions.answer: Simple things, mostly. Time with people I love, a good book, a quiet evening after a productive day. I've realised over time that lasting [[contentment]] rarely comes from big events, but from small, everyday moments.

questions.q: What made you happy when you were a child?
questions.answer: Very simple pleasures, honestly. Flying kites on the roof, visiting my grandparents in the village and eating mangoes straight from their trees. Life felt [[blissfully]] uncomplicated back then, with no deadlines or responsibilities to worry about.

questions.q: Do you think money can buy happiness?
questions.answer: Only up to a point. Having enough to live comfortably certainly reduces stress, but beyond that, relationships and purpose matter far more. Some of the most cheerful people I know, like my grandmother, live very [[frugally]] indeed.

questions.q: Do you think people are happier now than in the past?
questions.answer: It's hard to say. Life is certainly more comfortable, but people seem more stressed and constantly [[compare themselves]] with others online. My grandparents had far less, yet they seem more at peace than many young people I know.
